title: *The Critical Release of the CPI Report* FED RATES
speaker: Kevin Paffrath (Meet Kevin)

macro_themes.view: Headline 0.6% m/m matched but core printed ~0.335% vs 0.2% expected, a ~3.5-sigma miss with broad-based pressure (50% of categories at 3%+ y/y, supercore 0.42%).
Odds of an October hike jumped from 23% to ~50% and the market now prices ~3.86 more hikes to a Sept 2027 peak; Waller's dovish talk now looks cheap.
10-year rubber-banded above his 5.27% line to ~5.31%; only an Iran deal is likely to calm it.

macro_themes.theme: Iran deal is the only bailout
macro_themes.view: A deal in the Oct 20-27 window would let the Fed look through war-driven inflation; no deal means more hikes, possibly October and December.
Real average hourly earnings -0.7% y/y signal weakening consumers and eventual layoffs that could end the party.
In a rising-rate world cash-rich companies like Apple outperform while indebted ones like CoreWeave suffer.

calls.condition: If an Iran deal comes (Oct 20-27 window), buy the dip at support; if no deal, probably don't buy the dip.
calls.reason: Hot CPI raises hike odds; peak fear (QQQ ~700) is behind them, but this isn't a dip worth buying; the outcome hinges on an Iran deal.
calls.quote: peak fear is indeed still behind us... this isn't the level where I want to buy the dip because it's not much of a dip

calls.condition: Yields only chill out if an Iran deal happens; otherwise hikes keep pressure on.
calls.reason: Hot core CPI pushed the 10-year through his 5.27% line; he hopes it fades but sees only an Iran deal calming yields.
calls.quote: we have still rubber banded above that 5.27. Now, I hope this fades today because 5.312 is high

calls.condition: Long-term bullish case needs Warsh replaced ~2030 by a money-printing Fed chair.
calls.reason: Gold peaked with Warsh and won't rise even on hot CPI; it's not a hedge while the Fed isn't printing; wants it again after 2030.
calls.quote: even on a hot CPI report, you can't get this crap to go up. It's It's not a hedge anymore

calls.reason: Cash-rich companies benefit when rates rise; Apple was rising on the hot CPI while indebted names fell.
calls.quote: as usual, the cash-rich companies are doing the best. That's Apple.

notes: No date spoken; CPI day — the David Lin video states CPI came out Wednesday Oct 14, so this stream is likely 2026-10-14 (listing says 10-15). CoreWeave mentioned as indebted laggard but no explicit call; TLT (~77-78 bottom since Oct 8) mentioned only as context.
